newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Zambian presidential poll not corrupt, OAU.
newsitem.headline: Zambian presidential poll not corrupt, OAU.

text.p: The Organisation of African Unity (OAU) said on Monday last month's Zambian presidential polls, disputed by the opposition and criticised by western donors, were peaceful and without corruption.

"The voting was unfettered and there was no perceptible evidence of any attempt to influence or corrupt voters on the election day despite the fact that in some polling stations some voters did not know how to vote and had to be assisted," the report said.

Most western donors, who underwrite annual lifeblood aid to the southern African nation, say the elections, boycotted by some opposition parties, were irregular because of controversial constitutional amendments earlier in the year.

As a result of a new constitution passed this year former president Kenneth Kaunda was barred from contesting the election because his parents were Malawian. His UNIP party led the boycott of the polls.
Other opposition parties also refused to accept results of the election of which President Frederick Chiluba was declared winner.
Four opposition parties have since filed court petitions challenging Chiluba's landslide win.
They charged Chiluba lied about his nationality when he filed electoral nomination papers, and said they had evidence that he was of foreign parentage.

Two other parties, Agenda for Zambia and National Congress, filed a petition challenging the legitimacy of the poll. They claimed an impaired voters' register, which excluded half of the 4.6 million eligible voters, and other irregularities, including vote buying, rendered the elections illegal.

The Supreme Court early this month threw out opposition petitions challenging Chiluba's origins because they were filed prematurely. Under new laws, electoral petitions can only be made after an election has been held.
The elections office on Friday released final results from the poll showing that Chiluba won 69 percent of the presidential vote with 913,770 of the 1,258,805 votes cast.
